about: Where measures sit in each taxonomy (server/seed/data/taxonomies/; GLOSSARY.md). A measure is one thing measured in one place: it has one placement per taxonomy and its series always follow it; its key is its Abstract category and its name, so the Abstract placement's category is the key's path; where the Statistical Abstract prints a measure's series in two subsections, they are two measures, which may share a name (MEASURES in server/lib/series-dimensions.js). A placement is { category, basis, tables | reason }: basis 'table' when an Abstract table prints the measure's own data, from the same publisher (its table numbers; the table must be printed in that category); 'judgement' when GovGraph chose (a sentence saying why, naming the nearest table where there is one). { left_out: true, reason } keeps one out of a taxonomy on purpose. In the Abstract no two measures with the same name share a subsection; in another taxonomy they may, and are shown as one. Checked by server/lib/taxonomies.test.js; see features/taxonomies.
